Consult Summary:
- 45-year-old woman with acute onset pleuritic right-sided back pain, new cough with two episodes of hemoptysis, subjective fever and dyspnea today; suspected chest infection/pneumonia — advised urgent face-to-face assessment today for clinical examination and further management.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Acute shortness of breath and pleuritic pain localized to the right side of the back when taking deep breaths (started today).
  - Cough with blood on two occasions (hemoptysis) today.
  - Subjective fever (felt warm; assessed by patient using back of hand).
  - Palpitations/awareness of heart beating.
  - Increasing fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance for approximately 2 weeks; daily activities more difficult.
- Timeline:
  - Tiredness and reduced exercise tolerance: ~2 weeks.
  - Acute cough, pleuritic right-sided back pain, subjective fever, and hemoptysis: started today.
  - Methotrexate last taken this morning.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Deep inspiration exacerbates the right-sided back pain.
  - No relieving factors documented.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - Cough with hemoptysis x2.
  - Subjective fever.
  - Palpitations and fatigue.
  - Denies prior history of venous thromboembolism (no known clots in legs or lungs).
  - No family history of blood clots reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No other chronic diagnoses reported.
  - No medication allergies.
  - Non-smoker.

Past Medical History:
- Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
  - Patient reports ongoing treatment with methotrexate for SLE (no complications documented).

Medications:
- Methotrexate — dose/route/frequency not documented; last dose taken this morning.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Lives alone in a flat.
- Occupation: office-based desk job.
- Pets: cat in the home.
- Smoking: denies tobacco use.
- Alcohol/substance use: not documented.

Family History:
- No family history of blood clots reported.
- No other family history documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals:
  - Heart rate estimated by patient counting with clinician guidance: approximately 66–74 bpm (remote estimate).
  - No blood pressure, temperature (objective), or oxygen saturation recorded.
- Remote examination findings:
  - Capillary refill / finger perfusion appeared normal on remote fingertip test.
  - Oropharynx visualized remotely; no specific abnormality reported.
  - Patient self-palpation of neck: no enlarged glands felt.
  - Clinician impression: limited remote examination; patient did not appear acutely unstable on video assessment.
- No chest auscultation performed (face-to-face exam recommended).

Investigations:
- No imaging or laboratory tests performed during this consultation.
- No chest X-ray or blood tests performed or available.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute suspected chest infection / pneumonia with hemoptysis
  - Assessment: Clinical presentation suggests possible chest infection or pneumonia (acute onset cough, feverish symptoms, pleuritic chest pain, hemoptysis).
  - Plan:
    - Arrange urgent face-to-face review today for full clinical assessment.
    - At face-to-face visit: perform chest auscultation, measure blood pressure, pulse, temperature, and oxygen saturation.
    - Assess need for antibiotic therapy; start antibiotics if indicated after in-person assessment.
    - Consider chest X-ray if examination or clinical course warrants, or if symptoms do not settle on follow-up.
    - Do not prescribe antibiotics remotely prior to in-person assessment (no prescription issued during this consult).
    - Patient instructed to contact support team / reception to be booked into clinic today (support team phone number to be left in notes).
- Issue 2: Hemoptysis (two episodes)
  - Assessment: Hemoptysis present; severity and source unclear remotely.
  - Plan:
    - Evaluate in person during urgent clinic visit (as above).
    - Consider investigations (CXR, further imaging or labs) if indicated by in-person assessment or persistence/worsening of symptoms.
- Issue 3: Immunosuppression — Methotrexate use for SLE
  - Assessment: Patient taking methotrexate (last dose this morning); may be relevant to infection risk (not further specified in transcript).
  - Plan:
    - Document methotrexate use and last dose in clinic notes for in-person clinician review.
    - Review need for additional infection precautions or modification of immunosuppressive therapy as clinically indicated by in-person assessment (decision to be made by examining clinician).
- General plan items:
  - Urgent face-to-face GP assessment today is arranged via support team booking.
  - No remote prescription issued pending in-person assessment.
  - Possible follow-up chest X-ray or further investigations depending on examination and clinical course.
  - Reassure patient that isolated acute presentation is more suggestive of infection than malignancy, but further evaluation is required.

  - Objective vital signs: blood pressure, measured temperature, oxygen saturation not recorded.
  - Formal auscultation of lungs not performed.
  - No laboratory tests (CBC, inflammatory markers) or imaging (chest X-ray) available.
  - Methotrexate dose, route, frequency not documented.
  - Alcohol and broader substance use history not documented.
  - Clarification of patient name: conflicting names recorded (see conflicts).
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Patient initially identified as "Tracy Chapman" and later as "Doris" — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Consultation audio/transcript generally clear and intelligible; remote limited examination appropriately documented.
